questions.question: The unit of electric flux is represented by which quantity derived from the product of electric field and surface area?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton m² per coulomb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Electric Flux** is defined as the total number of **electric field lines** passing through a given **surface area** in a unit of time.
 
• It is a **scalar quantity** that describes the strength and distribution of the electric field over a surface.
 
• The mathematical formula for electric flux is the product of the **electric field** (E) and the **component of the area** (A) perpendicular to the field: Phi_E = E · A · costheta .
 
• The SI unit of the **electric field** is **Newton per coulomb** (N/C).
 
• The SI unit of **surface area** is **square meters** (m²).
 
• By multiplying the units of the electric field and area, the resulting unit of **electric flux** is (Newton/Coulomb) × square meters, which is **Newton m² per coulomb**.
 
• The unit can also be represented as **Newton m² C−¹**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Weber**: This is the SI unit of **magnetic flux**, not electric flux. It is equivalent to one Tesla-square meter.
 
• **Tesla**: This is the SI unit of **magnetic field strength** or magnetic flux density.
 
• **Joule**: This is the SI unit of **energy** or **work**, defined as the work done by a force of one Newton over a displacement of one meter.
 
• **Volt-meter**: Since the electric field can also be measured in **Volts per meter** (V/m), electric flux can alternatively be expressed in **Volt-meters** (V × m).
 
• The **dimensional formula** for electric flux is [ML³T−³A−¹].

questions.question: Which of the following is a moderator commonly used in nuclear reactors?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __All of the above__**

 **
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 
 __Key Points__
 
 **

__
 
• **Nuclear Moderator__**
 __
 
• A moderator is a material used in a nuclear reactor to slow down **fast neutrons__** produced during fission.
 
• Slow-moving neutrons, known as **__thermal neutrons__**, are more likely to cause further fission in **__Uranium-235__** nuclei, sustaining the chain reaction.
 
• Commonly used moderators include:
 __
 
• **Graphite__**: Used in many early reactors and modern gas-cooled reactors.
 
• **__Water (Light Water)__**: The most widely used moderator in commercial power plants (PWR and BWR).
 
• **__Heavy Water (Deuterium Oxide)__**: Used in reactors like CANDU because of its low neutron absorption.
 
 
 
 

 **
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 
 __Additional Information__
 
 **

__
 
• **Heavy Water (D₂O)__**
 __
 
• Consists of **deuterium__** (an isotope of hydrogen) instead of regular hydrogen.
 
• It is highly efficient because it has a very low **__neutron absorption cross-section__**, meaning it slows neutrons without capturing them.
 
 
 
• **__Graphite__**
 __
 
• Graphite is a form of **carbon__** that possesses high thermal stability and good moderating properties.
 
• It was used as the moderator in the world's first artificial nuclear reactor, **__Chicago Pile-1__**.
 
 
 
• **__Control Rods vs. Moderators__**
 __
 
• While moderators **slow down__** neutrons, **__control rods__** are designed to **__absorb__** neutrons to regulate or stop the reaction.
 
• Materials like **__Boron__** and **__Cadmium__** are commonly used for control rods.
 
 
 
• **__Coolants__**
 __
 
• A **coolant__** carries away the heat generated by the fission reaction to produce steam.
 
• In many reactors, **__water__** or **__heavy water__** serves the dual purpose of both **__moderator__** and **__coolant__**.

questions.question: Which is the primary source of helium on Earth, accumulating in natural gas deposits as a result of nuclear decay processes over millions of years?

options.text: Radioactive decay of uranium and thorium

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radioactive decay of uranium and thorium**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary source of **helium-4** on Earth is the **alpha decay** of heavy radioactive elements, specifically **uranium** and **thorium**, found in the Earth's crust.
 
• During the process of **radioactive decay**, these heavy nuclei emit **alpha particles**, which are essentially **helium nuclei** consisting of two protons and two neutrons.
 
• Over millions of years, these alpha particles capture electrons from their surroundings to become stable **helium atoms**.
 
• Because helium is a **non-reactive noble gas**, it migrates through the crust and becomes trapped in **impermeable rock formations**, often accumulating in the same reservoirs as **natural gas** (methane).
 
• **Photosynthesis** is incorrect as it is a biological process that produces **oxygen** and glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• **Cosmic rays** interact with the upper atmosphere to produce small amounts of **helium-3** and tritium, but they are not the source of the vast underground helium deposits used commercially.
 
• **Mantle convection** refers to the physical movement of the Earth's mantle due to heat, which helps transport gases but is not the **nuclear process** that generates helium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Helium** is the second most abundant element in the **observable universe**, but it is relatively rare on Earth because it is light enough to escape **Earth's gravity** and leak into space.
 
• Most of the world's commercial helium is extracted through **fractional distillation** of natural gas, where helium concentrations can reach up to 7 percent.
 
• The **United States**, **Qatar**, and **Algeria** are among the top global producers of helium.
 
• Helium is critical for **high-tech applications**, including cooling **superconducting magnets** in **MRI scanners**, manufacturing **semiconductors**, and as a lifting gas for balloons and airships.
 
• Because it is produced over geological timescales (millions of years) and escapes into space once released, helium is considered a **non-renewable resource**.

questions.question: _________ translates a low level language program into Machine Code
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assembler**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **assembler** is a program that translates assembly language code into machine code.
 
• **Assembly language** is a low-level programming language that is closely related to machine code but is more readable for humans.
 
• Assembly language uses **mnemonics** for operations and addresses, making it easier to program than binary machine code.
 
• The **machine code** output by the assembler can be directly executed by the computer's CPU.
 
• Assemblers are crucial for programming embedded systems and other low-level hardware components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Compiler**__

 __
 
• A **compiler** translates high-level programming languages (like C, C++, or Java) into machine code.
 
• Unlike assemblers, compilers deal with more abstract and complex code structures.
 
• Compilers perform various optimization techniques to make the code run efficiently.
 
 
 
• **Interpreter**__
 __
 
• An **interpreter** executes instructions written in a programming or scripting language directly, without needing them to be compiled into machine code first.
 
• Languages like Python and JavaScript often use interpreters.
 
• Interpreters are generally slower than compiled programs because they translate code on-the-fly.
 
 
 
• **Virus**__
 
 
• A **computer virus** is a type of malicious software that, when executed, replicates by inserting copies of itself into other computer programs, data files, or the boot sector of the hard drive.
 
• Viruses often cause harmful effects, such as corrupting data or taking control of the system.
 
• They are not related to the process of translating programming languages.

questions.question: Which among the following is the procedure to view digital signature details in MS PowerPoint?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• To view the details of a digital signature in MS PowerPoint, navigate to the **File tab**.

• In the Info panel, locate and click the **View Signatures** option to access the digital signature details.
 
• This process allows users to verify the authenticity and integrity of the signed document.
 
• Digital signatures provide security assurances by confirming the document's origin and ensuring it has not been tampered with.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• A digital signature is a cryptographic technique used to authenticate the identity of the signer and ensure the document's integrity.
 
• It is widely used in legal, financial, and official documents to provide a secure and tamper-proof way of document verification.
 
 
 
• **Steps to Add a Digital Signature in MS PowerPoint:**
 
 
• Go to the File tab and select **Protect Presentation**.
 
• Choose **Add a Digital Signature** and follow the prompts to sign the document.

questions.question: In Windows OS, which of the following actions will permanently delete a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Press Shift + Delete**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pressing **Shift + Delete** bypasses the Recycle Bin and permanently deletes a file from the system.
 
• This action removes the file from the file system table, making it inaccessible to the user unless recovery methods are employed.
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a feature in Windows OS that stores deleted files temporarily until manually cleared.
 
• Files deleted using **Shift + Delete** cannot be restored through the Recycle Bin.
 
• For accidental permanent deletion, specialized data recovery software may be required to retrieve the file.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Recycle Bin in Windows OS**

 
 
• The Recycle Bin is a special folder where deleted files are temporarily stored.
 
• Users can restore files from the Recycle Bin unless the bin has been emptied or files are deleted permanently using Shift + Delete.
 
• The Recycle Bin can be customized to allocate a specific amount of storage space for deleted files.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Deletion**
 
 
• Permanent deletion bypasses temporary storage locations like the Recycle Bin.
 
• It removes file references from the file system, but the actual data remains on the storage device until overwritten.
 
• Tools like disk shredders can be used to overwrite deleted files, ensuring complete erasure.
 
 
 
• **Data Recovery**
 
 
• Data recovery tools like EaseUS or Recuva can retrieve files that have been deleted permanently, provided the data has not been overwritten.
 
• Recovery is more successful if attempted promptly after deletion.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts in Windows**
 
 
• Shift + Delete: Permanently deletes a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin.
 
• Ctrl + C and Ctrl + V: Copy and paste files or content.
 
• Alt + Tab: Switch between open windows.
 
• Ctrl + Z: Undo the last action.

questions.question: The PCB (typically used as a baseboard for assembling electronic components) stands for :
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is** ​Printed Circuit Board.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **A printed circuit board (PCB) **is a structure that assembles and connects electronic components into a unified circuit, enabling the flow of electrical current between them.
 
• The base of a PCB is typically made from a rigid, nonconductive material, though it can also be made from flexible or a combination of rigid and flexible materials.
 
• Components like diodes, inductors, and transistors are attached to the PCB, and electrical traces connect these components.

Types of PCB Layers:

 
• **Single-layer PCBs** are used in simple devices like home appliances.
 
• **Double-layer PCBs** offer greater component density and are used in applications such as automotive dashboards or LED lighting.
 
• **Multilayer PCBs **are common in more complex hardware like computer graphics cards and motherboards.

Modern PCBs typically consist of the following four layers:

 
• **Substrate: **The core layer, usually a rigid insulating material like FR-4 (a fiberglass/epoxy composite). Flexible substrates, often made from plastic, can bend to fit space requirements and withstand higher temperatures and harsh conditions. Some PCBs combine both rigid and flexible substrates.
 
• **Conductive Layer: **Typically made from a thin sheet of copper. Single-sided PCBs have one conductive layer, while double-sided PCBs have two—one on each side of the substrate. Multilayer PCBs alternate between substrate and conductive layers.
 
• **Solder Mask: **A nonconductive layer that covers the conductive material, giving PCBs their characteristic green color (though other colors can be used). The solder mask insulates the underlying traces etched in the conductive layer and is also applied to the bottom of single-sided PCBs.
 
• **Silkscreen:** The topmost layer, consisting of labels that include numbers, letters, symbols, or other information to indicate the functions of each connection point. This labeling is typically white but can be in other colors as well.

questions.question: A temporary storage area, attached to the CPU, for Input / Output operations, is called as ______.

• **A temporary storage area, attached to the CPU, for Input/Output operations is called a Buffer.**
 
• A buffer is a temporary storage area that holds data while it is being transferred between two locations.
 
• Typically, it is used to accommodate the difference in speed between the CPU and other components, such as input/output devices.
 
• Buffers help manage data flow, ensuring smooth and efficient data transfer and processing, preventing bottlenecks, and accommodating differences in data transfer rates.

• File: A file is a container in a storage system, like a hard drive, used for storing data permanently. It is not a temporary storage area attached to the CPU.
 
• Register: Registers are small, fast storage locations within the CPU used for immediate data manipulation and processing. While they are temporary storage, they are not specifically for input/output operations.

questions.question: Which of the following MS-Excel functions returns a number rounded up, away from zero, to the nearest multiple of significance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CEILING( )**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CEILING():** This function rounds a number up, away from zero, to the nearest multiple of significance. 
 
• The "**significance**" represents the multiple to which you want to round the number. 
 
• For example, if you have a number like 4.1 and you wanted to round up to the nearest whole number, you would use **CEILING(4.1, 1)** and it would **return 5**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ROUND(): **This Excel function round off numbers to a specified number of digits. It follows the standard rules of rounding numbers. If the next digit to the specified number of digits is 5 or above, it rounds up; if it's less than 5, it rounds down. For example, **ROUND(2.15, 1)** would **return 2.2**.
 
• **CELL(): **This function in Excel is used to get information about the formatting, location, or contents of a particular cell. It doesn't round numbers. It has two parts, first is the info-type e.g. address, row, col, etc. which represents what information you want to fetch and the second is optional, which refers to the reference cell.
 
• **FLOOR():** **Similar to the CEILING function**, the **FLOOR function in Excel rounds a number down (towards zero)**, to the nearest multiple of significance. For example, **FLOOR(4.7, 1**) would **return 4**.

**Remember, both the FLOOR and CEILING functions will round towards or away from zero (negative values inclusive), respectively. For rounding strictly down or up (ignoring zero), Excel uses FLOOR.MATH and CEILING.MATH.**
